description: Tutorial lesson T3 (Get Movin'), mouse+keyboard player path: menu -> picker -> lesson boots from tutorial_postdeploy -> disembark the Boyz+Warboss from the Battlewagon via the real row-click + ConfirmationDialog + 11 placement clicks inside the 3-inch ring -> the boyz_move_after_disembark step teaches that the disembarked unit still gets its own move because the wagon has not moved yet (drag a Boy, End This Unit's Move) -> at that step, asserts the T-094 per-model 2" coherency rings are NOT drawn (a player reported the 10 overlapping cyan circles around the just-disembarked mob as an unexplained busy 'engagement range' bubble) while the red enemy ER rings, the green reach circle container and the live P3-116 ghost coherency preview all still work; then, mid-carry, asserts the REPLACEMENT affordance - exactly ONE CarriedCoherencyRing tracking the ghost, radius = the carried base radius + the edition's coherency distance, thin stroke, wearing its cyan OK colour on a coherent drop - and that it is gone again after the drop -> Advance the Battlewagon through the mode radio + Confirm Movement Mode gate -> move the hull in TWO drags (asserting the second adds to the first, which is what the step now tells the player) -> turn it with Q held mid-drag on the 'POINT IT RIGHT!' step -> End This Unit's Move -> End Movement Phase under a strict spotlight -> summary, completion persisted, back to menu.

steps.comment: OK on the native ConfirmationDialog - its internal button has no scene path for click_node
19.03: the attached Warboss disembarks WITH the Boyz. Before the fix the placement only asked for the 10 Boyz, reported complete, and left the Warboss aboard.
The Warboss model is actually ON THE BOARD at a placed position, not merely flagged as disembarked
Battlewagon is empty — neither the Boyz nor the Warboss are left inside
11e 18.04 - a tactical disembark from a transport that has NOT moved leaves the unit selected to make its own move; the new step teaches that affordance

PLAYER REPORT (Get Movin' step 4): beginning the disembarked Boyz' move used to paint one cyan 2" coherency ring PER model - 10 overlapping ~5.3"-wide circles on a tightly-packed mob, which players read as an unexplained engagement-range bubble. The rings are gone; the container stays (empty) so this assertion is meaningful rather than vacuous.

The OTHER two movement guides must survive the removal: the red enemy engagement-range rings (MovementERVisual) are still populated on move-begin, and the per-model green reach circle container (MoveRangeVisual, filled on pickup) still exists. Only the coherency rings are zeroed.

m1 sits at board (480,500) after placement. Carry it 120px (3") straight up FIRST - far enough that its nearest mate m2 at (544,500) is 136px away centre-to-centre, i.e. more than the 2" coherency distance once both 32mm bases are taken off - so the broken-coherency state can be inspected. PAUSED mid-flight (release:false); the carry then comes back to the 1" drop below before mouse_up_board stages it.
Proves the ring is live, not a static decoration: it recolours as the carry crosses out of coherency, from the same verdict that drives the label and the ghost lines.

Carry back to the intended 1" drop WITHOUT releasing - MovementController._unhandled_input routes any motion to _update_model_drag while dragging_model holds, so a buttonless hover moves the live carry. The ring must follow and flip back to cyan.
10-model mob -> 9 lines from the carried Boy to his mates, at least one of them green. This is the affordance that replaces the rings, so it is asserted in the same breath as their absence.

Follow-up to the ring removal: coherency came back as ONE ring on the model actually being carried, instead of T-094's one-per-model. This pins the count at 1, the anchor to the ghost, and the radius to base + coherency distance so an edition change to the 2" distance moves the ring with it.
The ring recolours from the same verdict as the label (cyan = coherent, amber = broken). Amber deliberately, not red - red is the enemy engagement-range rings.
and still no rings after the drop - the drag path must not re-introduce them either
staging a model must NOT advance the step - it waits for the move to be locked in
the Boy really moved - guards against a zero-distance stage passing for a move (staged moves only reach GameState on CONFIRM_UNIT_MOVE, so this reads the live move data)
confirming the move wrote the new position through to GameState
Keep Roll lives inside an embedded Window (AcceptDialog) - real-coordinate clicks into embedded windows are unreliable, the schema's emit_pressed escape hatch exists for this

steps.script:
var o = tree.root.get_node("/root/TutorialOverlay")
return o.current_body_text().contains("grab it again")
steps.comment: the card must actually SAY the move can be spent over several drags - players were treating the drag as one-shot and burning the whole move by accident
first hop - deliberately only part of the way, the second drag below proves the rest of the move is still there
the first hop is 60 board px = 1.5in of a 12in+D6 advance, i.e. a small fraction of the move - the second drag below is shown to ADD to this rather than replace it
the turn step must name the actual rotate keys - {key:rotate_left}/{key:rotate_right} render through KeybindingManager, so an unresolved token would read '{key:rotate_left}' and fail this
the wagon enters the step un-rotated, so the delta the step's done-leaf watches for is unambiguous

second hop AND the rotation in one grab: Q only rotates a model that is currently held (MovementController clears selected_model on drop), which is exactly what the step tells the player to do - grab, hold, tap Q/E, let go

steps.script:
var u = GameState.get_unit("U_BATTLEWAGON_T")
return abs(float(u.models[0].get("rotation", 0.0)) + PI / 6.0) < 0.01
steps.comment: two Q taps = -2 * PI/12 = -PI/6 rad (-30 degrees), i.e. the 15-degrees-a-tap the prompt promises

multi-step movement proven: two 1.5in hops read back as 3.0in, so the second drag ADDED to the first instead of replacing it - a replace would still read 1.5in here. This is exactly what step 6's new wording claims
